name: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur al-ʿAdwānī
summary: Basran reader and student of Abū al-Aswad, later judge in Khurasan, named with Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim among the first to dot the letters of the Qurʾān.
bio: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur learnt Arabic and the Qurʾān with Abū al-Aswad in Basra and stands in al-Zubaydī's second generation of Basran grammarians. He went east to Khurasan and served as judge in Merv; the sources tell that the governor al-Ḥajjāj sent him away from Iraq after he pointed out a mistake in the governor's speech.
With Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim he is credited with the dots that tell apart letters of the same shape in copies of the Qurʾān. He was also known as a transmitter of hadith.
uncertain: His year of death is given variously, before 90/708 or as late as 129/746.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 4 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
